newsitem.title: UK: Edinburgh picks bidders for two PFI hospital deals.
newsitem.headline: Edinburgh picks bidders for two PFI hospital deals.

text.p: Health authorities in the Scottish capital Edinburgh said on Wednesday they had selected preferred bidders for two large privately-financed hospital projects in the city, one led by construction groups BICC Plc and Morrison Plc and the other including private builder Millar and utility group Scottish Hydro-Electric Plc.

"It is hoped that after detailed design work and contract negotiations, full business cases from both trusts will be submitted to the Scottish Office and the Treasury by the first quarter 1997 and that the new hospitals will be ready by 2002," the authorities said in a statement.
The group picked as preferred bidder for the larger 180 million stg project, for a new Royal Infirmay at Craigmillar, is called Consort and includes the Royal Bank of Scotland Plc.
Facilities management elements in the proposal would be supplied by Haden F.M. and Initial Healthcare, part of the Rentokil Initial Plc group.

The second project, involving a 90 million spend over five years, is to rebuild the Western General Hospital on its existing site and expand its capacity to cope with an anitcipated 40 percent increase in patient numbers.
The Miller consortium picked for this work includes the privately owned construction company Miller Group, Building and Property Facilities Management Ltd, as well as Scottish Hydro.
Both projects involve new accommodation for research and teaching for the University of Edinburgh Medical School -- which has a reputation as one of Britain's best medical faculties.

Using the government-backed PFI (private finance intiative) scheme, large capital spending projects such as hospitals can be funded primarily from the private sector with subsequent lease-back contracts for the public sector users.
However, both the construction industry and some health services have criticised slow progress with hospital contracts.
